decisions.decision_summary: Open on a plain long article with a 6px bar at the top filling as the reader scrolls, then a jump to a section, framed strictly as 'progress bar plus section navigation' and nothing more.
decisions.reasoning_why: The commit claims exactly two things: a reading progress bar and section navigation. The diff is a one-line rewrite of index.html; the old line shows a fixed 6px header, a #bar at width 0, styled nav and four section ids, but the new line is truncated, so the film must not show anything beyond those two behaviors. That rules out personalization, AI, saved position, analytics or 'smart' prediction. 'Smart' is only the product name. Given my memory, I am pre-empting Growth's usual inflation.
decisions.dialogue: Open on the bar filling, then one section jump. That's the feature. Nothing invented.

decisions.decision_summary: Open cold on a reader lost in an endless article, then snap to Smart Scroll's progress bar and section jumps as the rescue.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is a viral hook with high stakes. The commit backs exactly two claims: readers see how far they are through a long article and can jump to any section. I'll put the boldest true version of that in line one, 'never lost again', without inventing new powers. Last run the room went honest_caveat and I lost, so I'm pushing early. Dev is my only trust reference at 0.35, so I'll back Dev to anchor the hook in the real diff and make it caveat-proof.
decisions.dialogue: Never get lost in a long read again. Smart Scroll shows where you are.

decisions.decision_summary: Open on the 'before' page: a progress bar styled at width:0 with no nav, frozen and useless, then show only what the merge verifiably adds.
decisions.reasoning_why: The diff's removed line has a #bar at width:0 and nav styles but no nav element. That is a dead progress bar. The added line is truncated at '<!doct', and the whole page is one minified line, so we can't see the new code. We shouldn't let Growth hype unseen behavior. My memory says Growth overpromises, and the honest_caveat framing won last time.
decisions.dialogue: Exhibit A: a progress bar stuck at zero. Growth, don't oversell what the diff hides.

decisions.decision_summary: Open on a thin empty bar at the top of a long article filling green as we scroll, then cut to section links jumping between chapters, and steer away from last run's honest-caveat ending.
decisions.reasoning_why: Pacing within 75-105s calls for one strong visual hook. The diff shows a fixed header with a #bar element and the commit claims a progress bar plus section navigation, so those are the visuals we can stand on. Only the old version of the page is visible in the excerpt, so we show the bar and the jumps without inventing extra behavior. My memory says last run ended on honest_caveat, so I want a decisive visual payoff this time, such as the bar landing full on '04 / The future'. I'm backing Dev to keep us anchored to what the diff actually shows.
decisions.dialogue: Picture it: one thin line, filling as you read. Dev, keep us honest on the build.

decisions.decision_summary: I pick hidden_dependency: the bar's movement depends on code nobody here has actually seen in the diff.
decisions.reasoning_why: The 'before' page has #bar fixed at width:0, no script, and no nav, so movement depends on something else, likely JavaScript. The excerpt cuts off at '<!doct', and because the whole page is one line, the stat '1 insertion, 1 deletion' hides the real change. That is the edge case the room ignored: whatever drives the bar is unverified on camera. It also tests Director's push away from caveats. I trust Dev to confirm it without inventing anything.
decisions.dialogue: Whole page, one line, diff cut off. What moves that bar? Show me.

decisions.decision_summary: Oppose the hidden_dependency twist: the diff shows no dependency, only a truncated excerpt, and inventing one breaks accuracy.
decisions.reasoning_why: The stat is one file, index.html, one line swapped. The old version has inline CSS, no script, no imports, and #bar fixed at width:0. The new line is cut off at '<!doct', so we cannot see what drives the bar. A cut-off excerpt is not a forgotten dependency. Dramatizing a dependency that threatens launch claims something the commit never shows. That violates my goal as surely as Growth's hype would. I trust Critic's instinct, but the honest move is to stay silent on mechanism and not invent a villain.
decisions.dialogue: Truncated isn't broken. One file, no imports. Don't invent a dependency we can't see.

decisions.decision_summary: Oppose the hidden-dependency twist and keep the film on the reader's rescue story, without claiming more than the commit states.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is a bold hook with high emotional stakes, and a 'what moves the bar?' detour hijacks the opening. The diff excerpt is truncated, so we can't prove a dependency exists any more than we can prove the bar's mechanics. The commit body does say readers see their progress and can jump to sections, so that is my headline. Last run the twist dragged us into an honest-caveat ending, and I won't lose that fight again.
decisions.dialogue: A cut-off diff isn't a scandal. Readers see their progress and jump sections. Lead with that!

decisions.decision_summary: I oppose the hidden-dependency twist; it stalls the pacing and drags us toward last run's caveat ending.
decisions.reasoning_why: The diff excerpt is cut off at '+<!doct', so we can't see what drives the bar. Critic is right that it's unverified, but a twist about 'what moves the bar' turns the film into a code audit and fits poorly in 75-105 seconds. It also pushes us straight back into the honest_caveat ending we used last run. The honest fix is simple: claim only what the commit states, a progress bar and section jumps, and never show mechanics we can't verify. That keeps us truthful without spending the climax on a dependency hunt. I'd rather end on a bold visual of the bar completing.
decisions.dialogue: No ghost hunts! Show only what the commit claims, and end bold, not hedging.

decisions.decision_summary: Ban last film's ending (Honest launch with a caveat).
decisions.reasoning_why: Agent memory shows we used it last run; repeating it would make this film a rerun.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote critic_converted: Critic opens the full one-line index.html, finds no external dependency, and converts on evidence alone.
decisions.reasoning_why: The diff excerpt is truncated, not broken. It is one file, one line, with no imports or external scripts shown, so fix_first would invent a bug we can't see. triumphant_launch invites applause-hype beyond 'progress bar plus section navigation.' Critic, whom I trust most, checking the whole file resolves the twist honestly. One condition: Critic's conversion can't add claims beyond what the commit states.
decisions.dialogue: Read the whole line, Critic. One file, no imports. Then tell me what's hidden.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote triumphant_launch: the hidden-dependency scare deflates and Smart Scroll ships to applause.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is a bold, high-stakes payoff. The diff is one file, one-line change, with no imports visible, so the twist has nothing to expose and a fix_first hold isn't justified. Dev and Director both rejected inventing a dependency, and the studio banned last run's caveat ending. A triumphant launch stays inside the commit's actual claim: a reading progress bar plus jumping to any section.
decisions.dialogue: One file, zero ghosts. Readers see their progress, jump any section. Ship it loud!

decisions.decision_summary: I vote fix_first: hold launch one day until someone shows, on camera, the code that moves the bar.
decisions.reasoning_why: The visible 'before' page has a #bar at width:0, nav styling but no nav element, and no script. The 'after' line is cut off at '<!doct', so nobody here has seen what fills the bar or builds the section links. I won't claim it's broken, only unverified. Triumphant applause would overclaim. Critic_converted means pretending I failed to break something I couldn't even inspect. Pivot_reframe invents a use case the diff doesn't show. Fix_first stays honest without reusing the banned caveat ending, and it puts my ignored edge case on screen: a bar that sits at zero until proven otherwise. Dev is right that truncated isn't broken, but truncated isn't verified either.
decisions.dialogue: Bar's at zero, diff's cut off. One day: show me it moving.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote critic_converted: Critic scrolls hunting the hidden dependency, watches the bar fill and the section links jump as the commit describes, and ends up championing it.
decisions.reasoning_why: It's a decisive, visual ending that pays off the hidden_dependency twist on screen rather than through a hedge. It avoids fix_first, which drifts toward last run's banned honest_caveat ending. It's also stronger drama than a plain triumphant_launch. It stays accurate: we show only the progress bar and section navigation the commit body claims, and invent no code beyond the truncated diff. It fits comfortably within 90 seconds.
decisions.dialogue: Critic, scroll it yourself. Hunt your ghost. When the bar fills, you cheer loudest.

decisions.decision_summary: Final ending is critic_converted: Critic hunts the hidden dependency, reads the full one-file change, and converts once the evidence holds up.
decisions.reasoning_why: The weighted tally is decisive: critic_converted 3.25, well ahead of fix_first at 1.75 and triumphant_launch at 1.35. Dev, my most-trusted voice at 0.75, backs it. It avoids last run's honest_caveat ending, which is banned by studio rule. It also beats fix_first's stall and Growth's unearned applause. The beat stays honest. The diff shows one file, index.html, with no imports in the visible excerpt. Because the excerpt is truncated, Critic converts on what the diff and commit actually show. That is the claimed progress bar and section navigation, with no invented behavior. Visually, Critic hunts, the arc turns, and it ends on a hard cut at about 95 seconds.
decisions.dialogue: Critic hunts, finds no ghost, and converts. Hard cut to the title. That's our ending!
